law: A WorkbenchSession is the single state bundle every workbench view operates on: sources, project, engine/profile, operation and view state. It is a client-side session model over the existing semantic authorities — it introduces no second semantic, type, project or format engine, and it mints no parallel identity vocabulary: every result binds the DX0 product-receipt-basis field set.

sources.binding: sourceRevisions (DX0 product-receipt-basis): the input basis and file revisions a result was computed from, under the existing input-basis and source-identity authority.
obligations: Multifile edits are authored, version-checked and atomic through the existing edit-transaction authority; cross-file and browser/native edits never bypass it.
A result computed from old source revisions is stale and is rejected, not published as current.
Engine-profile or framework switches re-key the session basis; results from the previous basis are invalidated, not reinterpreted.

project.binding: projectConfiguration (DX0 product-receipt-basis): project identity plus configuration facts — tsconfig/paths, .verterrc.json, lint preset, vite-config trust state, framework profile.
obligations: Project-model derivation stays with its existing producing owner (PM0 line); the session records, never derives, project truth.
An old-project result on a changed project configuration is stale and rejected.
Browser sessions hold the project snapshot through the BWH platform-host io service (host-provided virtual workspace); no hidden source upload leaves the session.

engineProfile.binding: engineIdentity and hostIdentity (DX0 product-receipt-basis): engineIdentity is the engine kind and exact version — playground typescript@6.0.3 pin, verter-tsc tsgo pin, or the resolved provider engine; hostIdentity is the executing host — the browser runtime and WASM build selector, or the explicitly selected native companion binary and version.
obligations: Execution class follows DX0 host-execution-class.v1: Portable runs in the browser sandbox; NativeOnly runs only through explicitly selected local-native execution (DX4/DX5 companion); ExternalOwner engines are pinned, provisioned and bound, never embedded.
Version selection is explicit and disclosed on every result; a result must not be presented under an engine it did not run on.
No hidden replacement engine: substituting a different engine never makes an execution class true.

operation.binding: completenessState (DX0 product-receipt-basis): complete, complete-empty, partial, pending, unsupported, ambiguous, failed, cancelled, stale. Every workbench operation result carries one, and complete-empty (a successful empty answer) stays distinct from every non-complete state.
obligations: Every operation result is source-linked and carries its answer-rail label; inspection-rail evidence never substitutes a semantic-rail answer.
Future capabilities return the distinct future/unsupported state with their named producing node — never successful empty output.
Cancellation stops additional irrelevant work, releases retained handles, and reports cancelled — not failed, not complete-empty.
Partial and pending are reported truthfully; dropped diagnostics or weakened typing to meet timing are forbidden.

view.binding: View state selects the presented matrix row (feature family, operation, output mode); it is presentation only and never becomes semantic truth.
obligations: Closed or disabled views create no background semantic work; rich information is fetched on demand under reduced client capabilities.
A view never presents stale-basis results as current; wrong-result-handle outputs are rejected.
The view layer may not invent feature rows: the presented feature set is generated from the feature matrix, not a hand-written tab list (PG2 owns the cutover).
Reduced-client rendering preserves semantic meaning: the same result and explanation are available, possibly with reduced presentation.

sessionRules: The session is the unit of sharing and reproduction: a shared or exported session (PG12) carries its full receipt basis — source revisions, project configuration, engine and host identity, and the operation/view state needed to replay it.

Snapshot basis is canonical and immutable: an observation names the exact basis it was computed on, and replay compares incremental and fresh execution on the same basis (owned downstream, not fabricated here).
The session model adds no orchestration system: scheduling, batching and host services stay with their existing owners (scheduler, BWH platform-host services).
Theme, layout and other presentation state ride the session but never gate semantic availability.
